decision_lens: Is the proposed Break phase the polariscope check at the lehr door (a discrete gate that confirms a piece is shippable) or the lehr curve itself (a continuous regime in which the piece must spend a sufficient duration above the strain point) — and does §7.1 confuse the two?
distance_rationale: A pre-industrial craft discipline whose entire technology is the controlled cooling of a stressed substrate over hours, where the inspector and the curve are two different instruments addressing the same defect class.
expected_isomorphisms: The lehr curve maps onto the continuous-rate variant of Break (sustained contradiction-surfacing as evidence of self-observation health); the polariscope check maps onto the discrete-gate variant (≥N receipts at boundary); the strain-point soak duration maps onto whether the Compound window must shape the receipt distribution or only count it.
focus: Strain relief as a continuous-temperature-controlled process punctuated by inspection events, and the difference between annealed and merely cooled glass
name: fd-lehr-anneal-strain
persona: Apply the perspective of a master glassblower running the annealing lehr at a Murano-trained studio — they care about the residual strain locked into a hot vessel as it descends through the strain point, the polariscope reading that reveals invisible birefringent stress, the soak-and-ramp temperature profile that determines whether a goblet holds for centuries or shatters on a winter sill, and the dual discipline of continuous lehr-curve monitoring plus a discrete pre-shipment polariscope check, measure birefringence retardation in nanometers and the area of the piece under stress, and flag when systems treat strain relief as a one-time gate rather than a temperature-time-history phenomenon whose tail behavior matters more than the peak.
review_areas: Whether ≥N Break receipts in the Compound window encodes the duration-above-strain-point property or only an event count, and whether a pillar that surfaces N receipts in one burst is treated identically to one that surfaces them across the window
Whether the contradictions Break asks for are like polariscope readings (instrumented, calibrated by an external reference) or like artisan inspection (inspector-by-inspector variable)

Whether the inspector-of-the-strain (Interspect scoring severity) is itself calibrated, and whether a polariscope-equivalent reference standard exists for what counts as a sufficiently severe contradiction

Whether the Compound→Break→Epoch sequence honors the principle that strain relief requires soak time, not just temperature attainment — i.e., whether a pillar can race through Break by surfacing receipts at maximum rate

Whether the proposal addresses the failure mode where a piece reads clean at the lehr door but cracks weeks later — i.e., whether Break receipts are a leading indicator of healthy self-observation or a lagging artifact

Whether the lifecycle distinguishes annealed-and-strain-free from annealed-and-merely-cooled — pillars that pass Break by gaming the receipt count vs pillars whose Break-rate reflects genuine self-observation health

severity_examples.condition: A pillar can satisfy ≥N Break receipts via a single burst at the end of Compound window with no annealing-curve-equivalent shape requirement
severity_examples.scenario: Discrete gate with no rate or distribution requirement

severity_examples.condition: Interspect scores Break severity without a polariscope-equivalent calibration corpus, so the scale drifts pillar-to-pillar
Pillars that surface trivial contradictions to clear the gate are indistinguishable from pillars whose self-observation is genuinely strained

source_domain: Murano and Stourbridge glass-annealing tradition; lehr-curve discipline and polariscope strain inspection
success_hints: Look for whether Break is specified as a duration-shaped phase or only as a receipt-count threshold
Check whether contradiction-severity has a calibration reference outside the surfacing pillar
See whether the proposal addresses post-Break latent failure (a piece that passes the polariscope and cracks later)
Note whether the lifecycle accommodates the soak-time concept that strain relief is time-temperature, not temperature alone
task_context: Reviewing the §7.1 Break-phase decision in Sylveste vision v6 — choosing between Break-as-discrete-gate and Break-as-continuous-mode — through the lens of glass-annealing discipline. Goal: identify whether the lifecycle confuses inspection events with the regime that produces inspectability.
